anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Engine-level settings (memory pools, checkpoint cadence, log sizing, parallelism, etc.) are mis-calibrated with respect to hardware capacity and workload characteristics.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly: Sessions thrash on hot buffer pages and their associated latches, causing serialization and CPU spinning rather than true memory exhaustion.
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly: The write-ahead log path—log buffer, flush, switch, archive, replication retention—cannot keep pace with redo generation, stalling commits and checkpoints.

Composite definition: The database concurrently suffers from mis-tuned configuration parameters, severe buffer-cache/latch contention, and a saturated transaction-log subsystem. Together they create a feedback loop where write throughput is throttled at multiple layers while internal synchronization points become hot spots.

Combined anomalous phenomena: 1) Commit latency and overall response time spike, with wait-event views showing a mixture of log-flush waits, buffer-busy/page-latch waits, and background-writer or checkpoint waits. 2) CPU usage oscillates between idle gaps (when sessions sleep on I/O or log flush) and spin-loops (while contending for latches). 3) Checkpoints fire more frequently, ejecting dirty pages and intensifying latch contention on the buffer freelist, yet still fail to relieve log pressure because log files are undersized or archiver lagging. 4) Performance regressions appear immediately after a configuration change or version upgrade, but traditional resource monitors show disks and CPUs only partially utilized, making the root cause hard to isolate.

Causal chain: Undersized log segments or slow archiving lengthen commit flush times; administrators react by tightening checkpoint intervals or enlarging work-memory, inadvertently pushing more dirty pages into the buffer pool. The higher dirty-page churn amplifies contention on buffer hash chains and page latches, causing threads to spin and burn CPU without progress. The resulting stall lengthens transaction durations, which in turn sustains a higher volume of concurrent sessions and redo generation, keeping the log subsystem overwhelmed. Because the mis-set parameters (checkpoint cadence, buffer-pool size, parallelism, log buffer length) govern both the buffer manager and the log writer, their poor calibration creates circular amplification: slow log flushes trigger aggressive checkpoints; aggressive checkpoints raise latch contention; latch contention delays the very transactions that must flush the log, thereby deepening the bottleneck. Without correcting all three layers, tuning any single layer in isolation provides only transient relief.

entry.official_description: SSL parameters in CHANGE REPLICATION SOURCE are ignored because this MySQL replica was compiled without SSL support; they can be used later if MySQL replica with SSL is started
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with log shipping, replica apply state, replication-channel configuration, or cross-node communication needed to keep replicated state consistent.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver state, log retention, downstream apply lag, and network stability between replication endpoints.
